Connectors endpoint v2

Manage connectors — the source and destination integrations pipelines read from and write to.

Note: v3 available for Events and Pipelines

The Events and Pipelines endpoints now have v3 versions available. The Connectors, Transforms, and Webhooks endpoints remain on v2.

Create a connector

POST /v2/connectors

Name Type Required Description
typestringYesOne of postgres, s3, snowflake, kafka, webhook.
directionstringYessource, destination, or bidirectional (webhook only).
configobjectYesType-specific connection details, e.g. connection string or IAM role ARN.
create-connector.sh bash 
curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "type": "postgres",
    "direction": "source",
    "config": { "connection_string": "postgres://..." }
  }'

Rotate credentials

POST /v2/connectors/{id}/rotate — pauses every pipeline referencing this connector for the duration of the rotation, then resumes them automatically.

Shared connectors

A connector referenced by multiple pipelines is rotated once, for all of them. Check a connector's pipeline_count field before rotating during a busy window.

Health status

GET /v2/connectors/{id} returns a health field of healthy, degraded, or down.

Events endpoint v3

Query, filter, and replay events that have flowed through a pipeline. Base URL: https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3.

v3 is current

v3 ships with advanced filtering, improved batch operations, and better pagination. Upgrade from v2 or view v2 docs.

List events

GET /v3/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/events — cursor-paginated with advanced filtering by type, status, and occurred_at range.

Name Type Required Description
typestringNoFilter to a single event type, e.g. order.created.
statusstringNoFilter by event status: success, failed, or dead_letter.
sincestringNoISO-8601 timestamp lower bound on occurred_at.
untilstringNoISO-8601 timestamp upper bound on occurred_at.
cursorstringNoOpaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor.
event.json json 
{
  "id": "evt_8f2c1a90",
  "type": "order.created",
  "status": "success",
  "occurred_at": "2026-08-18T09:12:44Z",
  "payload": { "order_id": "ord_4471" },
  "processing_time_ms": 143
}

Batch query events

POST /v3/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/events/query — Query events across multiple pipelines or with complex filter combinations in a single request (new in v3).

batch-query.sh bash 
curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines/events/query \\\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "filters": {
      "type": "order.created",
      "status": "failed",
      "since": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "limit": 100
  }'

Replay a dead-lettered event

POST /v3/events/{id}/replay — Re-runs an event that exhausted its retries from where it was dead-lettered. See the Error handling & recovery guide for when to use this versus reprocessing an entire time range.

Get a single event

GET /v3/pipelines/{pipeline_id}/events/{event_id} — Retrieve a single event by ID, including full processing history and error details if applicable.

Platform events

Lifecycle notifications like pipeline.started and connector.error are not returned by this endpoint — subscribe to them through the Webhooks endpoint instead.

Pipelines endpoint v3

Create and manage pipelines programmatically. Base URL: https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3.

v3 is current

v3 ships with improved error handling, batch operations, and enhanced filtering. Upgrade from v2 or view v2 docs.

Create a pipeline

POST /v3/pipelines

Name Type Required Description
namestringYesHuman-readable pipeline name, unique per workspace.
source_connector_idstringYesID of the connector events are read from.
destination_connector_idstringYesID of the connector events are written to.
transformsarrayNoOrdered list of transform step definitions. Omit for a pass-through copy.
schedulestringNoCron expression. Omit for event-triggered (streaming) pipelines.
error_handlingobjectNoError policy: retry, dlq, or discard. Defaults to retry.
create-pipeline.sh bash 
curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "ingest-orders",
    "source_connector_id": "conn_pg_orders",
    "destination_connector_id": "conn_snowflake_dw",
    "error_handling": {
      "policy": "retry",
      "max_attempts": 3
    }
  }'

List pipelines

GET /v3/pipelines — cursor-paginated with enhanced filter support. See Rate limits for the pagination envelope.

Batch operations

POST /v3/pipelines/batch — Create or update multiple pipelines in a single request. Available in v3.

Pipeline states

Returned pipelines include a state field of draft, active, or paused — see Pipelines for what each means.

Deleting a pipeline

Deleting a pipeline does not delete its source or destination connectors, and does not delete events already written to the destination. In-flight runs are allowed to finish before deletion completes.

Rate limits v2/v3

1,000
requests / minute

Default rate limit for standard-tier API keys, per workspace.

429
Status code

Returned when you exceed your rate limit.

60
seconds

Standard rate limit window.

See also: For complete details on plan tiers, quotas, and what happens when you exceed your limit, refer to Quotas & billing.

Rate limits apply to v2 and v3

These rate limits are shared across both v2 and v3 API versions. The Events and Pipelines endpoints are available in both v2 and v3, while other endpoints remain on v2.

Rate limit headers

Every response includes three rate-limit headers:

X-RateLimit-Limit
Request quota

Your rate limit for this window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining
Requests left

Remaining requests in the current window.

X-RateLimit-Reset
Window reset time

Unix timestamp when the limit resets.

A request over the limit returns 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header indicating seconds to wait.

Pagination

List endpoints (Pipelines, Connectors, Events) use cursor-based pagination — a departure from v1's offset-based pagination.

list-response.json json 
{
  "data": [ { "id": "pl_ingest_orders" } ],
  "next_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjIwfQ",
  "has_more": true
}

Error reference v2/v3

Error shape

error-response.json json 
{
  "error": {
    "code": "connector_unauthorized",
    "message": "The connector's credentials were rejected by the source system.",
    "request_id": "req_c93a10"
  }
}
Breaking change from v1

v1 returned bare error strings. v2 and v3 always wrap errors in an error object with a stable code field — match on code, not on message text.

Consistent across API versions

Error responses are identical in v2 and v3, including the Events and Pipelines endpoints available in both versions.
